_why: This script's whole job is to say NO WARNING when there is no warning, which means its catastrophic failure mode is the silent pass: a `findings()` that always returns [] reports every plugin CLEAN and looks exactly like a working check. So the mutations here are weighted toward loosening -- widening a key set, dropping a level of traversal, swallowing a parse error -- rather than toward breaking it noisily. Each mutation names the ONE test it is aimed at, so a kill by an unrelated assertion, a crash or a timeout is reported as a survivor with the actual catcher named rather than counted as ALL_CAUGHT. The `TestAgainstTheLiveBinary` class is deliberately NOT the named catcher for any key-set mutation: those tests compare TOP/MATCHER to the binary and would catch a widened set for the wrong reason, masking whether the recorded-warning tests -- the ones that pin what a USER saw -- still bite.

mutations.name: schema-becomes-an-allowed-top-level-key
mutations._mechanism: The exact fail-open this check exists to detect: widen TOP by the one key that was actually warning, and every recorded warning silently becomes CLEAN. This is also the mutation that proves the negative controls are load-bearing rather than decorative.

mutations.name: once-becomes-an-allowed-matcher-key
mutations._mechanism: The matcher-level half of the same fail-open. The bkit 2.0.8 line had TWO findings and only one of them was top-level; a check that sees only the top level reports the shorter message and reads as a partial fix.

mutations.name: matcher-traversal-is-dropped-entirely
mutations._mechanism: Not a widened set but a missing level: the top-level scan still works, so the script still WARNs and still exits 1 on the 2.0.8 shape. Only the exact recorded text catches it. A suite that greps for `$schema` instead of asserting the whole line lets this survive.

mutations.name: findings-always-returns-empty
mutations._mechanism: The total silent pass. Every plugin reports CLEAN, the CLI exits 0, and nothing crashes. The positive-control tests all still pass by construction -- that is the point of pairing them with negative controls.

mutations.name: plural-is-hardcoded-to-keys
mutations._mechanism: The recorded bkit 2.1.38 line is SINGULAR (`unknown key "$schema" ignored`). Hardcoding the plural is invisible to any assertion that only checks the key name, and it is how a replayed line stops matching the text a user would actually read.

mutations.name: unreadable-json-reports-clean
mutations._mechanism: `I could not read it` collapsing into `it is fine` -- the asymmetry this repo's handoff skill already enforces for the worktree comment and the state-file search. A malformed hooks.json would then exit 0.
mutations.find:
except Exception as exc:  # unreadable is NOT clean
        return ("UNREADABLE", label, str(exc))

mutations.name: warn-no-longer-sets-the-exit-code
mutations._mechanism: The check still PRINTS the warning and still looks right to a human reading stdout, but exits 0 -- so any CI gate or `&&` chain built on it passes silently. The mutation a screen-reading verification cannot see.

mutations.name: the-worst-exit-code-is-reset-each-iteration
mutations._mechanism: Exits 1 only when the LAST file warns. A single-file invocation -- which is how every manual run looks -- cannot distinguish this from correct behaviour.

mutations.name: truncation-limit-widens-to-fifty
mutations._mechanism: A transcription drift in `npn`. Only a key longer than 40 characters shows it, and real plugin keys are short -- so the corpus cannot catch this and the fixture must.

mutations.name: overflow-cap-off-by-one
mutations._mechanism: `bko` drifting from 5 to 6 changes both the listed keys and the `and N more` count. Six-finding configs are rare in the wild, which is exactly why this is fixture-only.

mutations.name: matcher-index-counts-from-one
mutations._mechanism: The site string is part of the recorded text (`hooks.SessionStart[0]`). An index base error renders a line that is wrong in a way no exit code and no key-name grep can see.

mutations.name: empty-findings-still-renders-a-line
mutations._mechanism: The emitter's early return is the entire reason a patched config produces NO warning. Removing it makes every clean plugin render `unknown keys  ignored` -- loud, but it inverts the check's meaning, and the positive controls are what notice.
